note: Independent rejudgment 2026-11-15 against RFC 1994 Section 4.1: "Because the Success might be lost, the authenticator MUST allow repeated Response packets during the Network-Layer Protocol phase after completing the Authentication phase." TestCHAPRepeatedResponseAfterSuccessKeepsSessionUp completes real LCP and accepted CHAP authentication, observes CHAP Success and the success event, then repeats the identical Response Identifier and 0x33 digest produced by readCHAPChallengeAndRespond after the session reached the network phase. It rejects every lifecycle event during the repeat and requires a subsequent LCP Echo-Reply, so a terminated or stalled session fails the scoped tolerance claim. The direct handler owns no misleading malformed-packet precondition; the auth backend deliberately accepts the stand-in digest. Read handleFrame/supportsProtocol/rejectUnsupportedProtocol: configured CHAP is tolerated without a Protocol-Reject or teardown outside the auth waiter. The single-positive annotation is justified for this repeated-input tolerance. Resending the previous CHAP reply Code is the separate RFC1994-4.1-9 obligation and remains an explicitly recorded gap; this verdict does not claim that behavior. The new valid LCP fixture leaves these assertions unchanged. No additional semantic coverage is inferred from a recorded producer-disabled panic.
